purpose: A current-main implementation assessment. This is intentionally separate from the formal acceptance ledger: it says what the code and fresh local checks establish, without promoting a release requirement early.

groups.reason: PostgreSQL partitions/RLS, retention, audit/outbox and the disposable backup/restore drill are implemented. One approved protected operations run must still retain current role-grant, audit-sink, WAL and isolated-PITR evidence.
The typed Stack renderer, isolation and bootstrap/teardown contracts exist. The current assembled runtime topology still needs a fresh physical Stack run with an attested image.

Role and renderer foundations exist, but the checked-in production Stack does not deploy the current durable runtime API or its complete trust wiring. Hosted role, RBAC, rollback and profile proof remain unfinished.
Fail-closed Firecracker/Jailer composition and a protected-run harness exist, but no Linux amd64 host with usable KVM, cgroups, reviewed fixtures and retained boot/cleanup evidence is available.
The Starlight site and generated references build locally. Publishing and checking the current revision on Pages is still an external publication step.
The public docs were improved and locally checked, but the complete coverage, snippet/spell gate, README smoke and claim-classification acceptance suites are not all present.
The codebase has the stated engineering boundaries and fresh local race tests pass, but the formal cross-repository standards evidence has not been assembled.

The project has useful local checks, but it does not yet retain complete red/green slice evidence, every promised command smoke, regeneration enforcement, CI-matrix evidence, or the final independent review.
Examples use the public SDK/HTTP boundary, but their complete formal static guard evidence is not current-head release evidence.
The example applications and selected local durable flows exist, but their full restart/reconnect/browser/TUI, Stack, sandbox/artifact, research and cross-example acceptance paths are not complete.
Approval authorization, denial and expiry exist, but policy invalidation while an Approval is pending is not implemented/proven.
Restart/replay behavior has historical local proof, but the required proof must be rerun against an attested current runtime image.
The seam and research are present, but the required supported subscription integration, credential lifecycle and protected live canary are not available.
Safe structured request logging and correlation foundations exist, but full OpenTelemetry telemetry, dashboards, alerting and correlated-session operator E2E are not complete.
Notifier configuration, redaction, retry and milestone-record code are covered locally. A current release completion record and delivery evidence are intentionally not claimed yet.
This is one MIT-licensed root Go module and its source is on main. The current local repository checks validate the layout.
The root module and direct-main workflow exist, but an immutable public release tag/external-consumer proof and complete machine-readable main-change evidence are not finished.

Fresh disposable PostgreSQL integration passed for the control and enrolled-host protocol: durable operations, tenant non-enumeration, idempotency/conflict, routing, reconnect, mTLS host delivery, receipt recovery, cleanup and reassignment.
There are control-plane implementations and focused tests, but the required hostile/execution/reaper/resource conformance evidence is not complete.
The operation ledger carries bounded output integrity metadata, but durable output content, backpressure and replay semantics are not implemented.
The unsafe local adapter acknowledgement/refusal contract and deterministic fake adapter lifecycle/clock suite are complete local development seams.
Capability negotiation, binding and regression refusal exist. No real protected capability can be advertised until its own profile evidence exists.
A black-box adapter suite passes for local-unsafe and fake adapters. It still needs the Firecracker adapter once a Linux/KVM profile can advertise a capability.
Admission validation/refusal foundations exist, but the required transfer, mount, secrets, proxy and hostile-environment data planes and conformance suites are not complete.
No volume/snapshot data plane or final security-profile release gate is implemented.

Fresh PostgreSQL multi-process host protocol proof covers enrollment, signed envelopes, restart, receipt recovery, quarantine and reassignment. Certificate rotation and the full durable output/lease conformance matrix remain.
The M3 authority and hostile-host protocol lane is implemented and freshly exercised. The required M4 Linux/KVM authority-boundary reproving has not happened.
Broker admission, approval and grants exist, but the canonical provider Tool-request parser and general JSON-schema validation are still missing.
The required sandbox adversarial and full local three-example Tilt E2E suites are not complete.
